title: Extract a list of unique departments from the employee list.
shortTitle: Extract a list of unique departments from the employee list
keyPoints: map(Employee::getDepartment) projects each employee to its department string
distinct() removes duplicates using equals() and hashCode(), keeping the first occurrence
distinct() is a stateful intermediate operation that internally tracks seen values in a Set
On a sequential stream distinct() preserves encounter order; on parallel, dropping order is faster
Collecting directly into a Set with toSet() gives uniqueness without a separate distinct() call
The classifier must not return null when used with distinct(), or downstream operations may fail

s1_definition.oneliner: `map` to the field, then `distinct()` to drop repeats, giving each unique value once.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **`map(Employee::getDepartment)`** projects each employee to its department string.
- **`distinct()`** removes duplicates by calling `equals()` and `hashCode()`, keeping only the first occurrence.
- **Stateful operation**: `distinct()` internally maintains a `Set` of seen values.
- **Order**: preserves encounter order on sequential streams; on parallel, `unordered()` is faster.
- **Alternative**: `collect(Collectors.toSet())` gives uniqueness without a separate `distinct()` call.
s1_definition.analogy: The HR manager at the National Bank of India wants the list of departments that actually exist, each named once, to plan an org chart. Many employees share a department, so she writes down each department the first time she sees it and ignores repeats. `map` plus `distinct` is exactly that.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Stream<Employee>
  [Rajesh/Loans, Priya/IT, Amit/Finance, Kavita/Loans, Suresh/IT]
       │
       │  .map(Employee::getDepartment)
       ▼
  Stream<String>
  ["Loans", "IT", "Finance", "Loans", "IT"]
       │
       │  .distinct()  (internal Set tracks seen values)
       │  Loans  → first time → keep
       │  IT     → first time → keep
       │  Finance→ first time → keep
       │  Loans  → already seen → skip
       │  IT     → already seen → skip
       ▼
  Stream<String>
  ["Loans", "IT", "Finance"]
       │
       │  .collect(toList())
       ▼
  List<String> [Loans, IT, Finance]
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
To get unique values of a field I combine two operations: I map each object to the field I care about, then I call distinct to remove the duplicates. For departments I mapped every employee to its department string, which produces a stream full of repeats because many people share a department, and then distinct kept only the first occurrence of each, giving me each department exactly once in the order it first appeared.

In my banking project at the National Bank of India this was building the definitive department list for a new org chart. The employee list had hundreds of people with the same department names repeating, so I projected to the department and applied distinct to collapse the repeats.

A senior point I always add is how distinct decides uniqueness: it relies on `equals` and `hashCode`. For strings this just works, but for custom objects I must override both properly. I also mention that distinct is stateful and keeps an internal set, and that collecting straight into a Set is simpler when I do not need encounter order.

Remember one sentence: `map(Employee::getDepartment).distinct()` projects and deduplicates in one pipeline, relying on equals and hashCode for uniqueness.
